stories.title: Benchmarking cell segmentation in two Spatialomics platforms with open-source software
stories.description: The in situ tissue microenvironment is a complex mixture of different cell types, microanatomic structures, and acellular matrix material. Further, disease perturbs the morphologies of these features significantly. Spatial proteomics utilizing optical or mass spectrometer imaging simultaneously detects expression and subcellular localization of many proteins. Accurate identification of heterogeneous, irregular, and tightly interdigitating cell boundaries is a crucial step for all downstream analyses, including cell phenotyping and cell-cell interaction networks. We describe a benchmarking approach for rapid assessment of segmentation algorithm performance in melanoma and breast cancer contexts using mass spectrometer and optical spatial omics imaging platforms. Comparison of cell segmentation by fourteen methods to pathologist ground-truth annotation with Jaccard pixel index and F1 object measurement identified Cellpose models that performed well across different tumor samples and data sources with minimal fine-tuning. Algorithms utilizing cell membrane and nuclear features demonstrated better performance in both tumor samples. This benchmarking approach is a rapid and effective method to assess performance of cell segmentation methods in different contexts for efficient algorithm selection and iterative model training.

stories.title: Conditional survival and dynamic prognostic nomogram for histologically defined anaplastic ganglioglioma: a SEER-based analysis
stories.description: Anaplastic ganglioglioma (AGG) is an extremely rare glioneuronal tumor with low incidence and heterogeneous survival patterns driven by a limited set of prognostic factors, and conditional survival has not been systematically evaluated in this entity. Patients histologically diagnosed with AGG between 2000 and 2022 were extracted from the SEER 17 registries. Age-adjusted incidence and annual percentage change (APC) were estimated by Joinpoint regression. Overall survival (OS) was analyzed with Kaplan–Meier curves and log-rank tests; 5-year conditional survival (CS) was computed at successive landmark times. Independent prognostic factors were identified by univariate and multivariate Cox regression. A CS-nomogram was constructed and evaluated by calibration plots, time-dependent ROC and C-index. Nomogram-derived risk scores were dichotomized using a cut-point selected on the basis of restricted cubic splines (RCS), and survival between strata was compared. A total of 143 AGG patients were identified, with 62 deaths during follow-up. Patients included pediatric (29.4%), AYA (38.5%), and adults ≥ 40 years (32.2%), and 64.3% were male; most tumors arose in cerebral lobes (73.4%). Age-adjusted incidence of AGG remained low throughout the study window, with crude annual rates of approximately 0.082 per 1,000,000 person-years. Five-year OS was 64.7%, while CS5 increased from 64.7% at diagnosis to 73.7% at 1 year, 82.5% at 2 years, and > 90% after 3 years. Multivariate analysis identified age ≥ 40, regional/distant stage, and multiple primary tumors as independent adverse factors. The CS nomogram showed good performance, with time-dependent AUCs > 0.75 and well-calibrated predictions, and risk stratification yielded significantly separated survival outcomes (P < 0.001). Long-term prognosis in AGG is highly dynamic: patients who survive the first three years acquire a substantially improved residual life expectancy. A CS-based nomogram, combined with RCS-guided risk stratification, translates this dynamic information into an individualized tool for counselling and risk-adapted surveillance.
